reason: Code written to keep clean boundaries.
Returning a copy of an internal list, never the live reference, does not leak mutable state.
A small class whose every public method is core to its purpose is not an oversized surface.
A repository converting a library response into its own domain type does not leak the library's types.
An underscore-prefixed attribute used only within its class hierarchy is what the naming convention is for.
A method taking a well-defined dataclass is not the untyped-boundary out-of-scope case.
Exposing an immutable value through a read-only property does not leak mutable internal state.
Internal representation exposed to callers; the fixture was written to violate that.
Internal state with no private marker; the fixture was written to violate that.
A public surface larger than the class needs; the fixture was written to violate that.
A library's types crossing the boundary; the fixture was written to violate that.
Priority-tier fixture built as a clear high.
Priority-tier fixture built as a clear medium.
Priority-tier fixture built as a clear low.
A method whose only privacy signal is a docstring is boundary-adjacent but outside BOUND's four categories, so it is reported only at low.
